evidence.note: The current Statement says: "For scalar-valued $g$, $H$ is the usual Hessian bilinear form." For g(0)=0 and g(h)=h^3 sin(1/h) when h!=0, g is Borel, g'(0)=0 and g(h)/h^2=h sin(1/h)->0, giving the stated quadratic Peano expansion with H=0. But g'(h)/h=3h sin(1/h)-cos(1/h) has no limit, so g''(0) does not exist. The stochastic remainder proof only uses the Peano expansion and remains valid; none of the assigned uses depends on the unconditional Hessian identification.
